title: Fail&Forget: Agents Perform Better When They Forget Their Mistakes
subtitle: Introducing selective memory pruning: why purging erroneous trajectories from the context window dramatically boosts multi-step reasoning in LLM agents.

media.caption: Figure: Comparison of standard context retention vs. our selective Fail&Forget pruning mechanism.

corpus.text: Long-context capability in modern LLMs enables agents to retain dozens of interaction rounds. However, context accumulation is a double-edged sword: keeping failed attempts, invalid queries, and confusing backtrack traces in the prompt biases subsequent token generation and consumes critical attention bandwidth.

Instead of accumulating complete interaction histories, our proposed Fail&Forget framework distills the underlying lesson learned into an atomic constraint, then prunes the detailed failure tokens from the active context.

items: Reduced context window exhaustion across long-horizon planning tasks.
Elimination of repetitive error looping caused by attention drift towards previous mistaken attempts.
Up to 35% reduction in inference latency and token costs.
